body.content: A decentralized network of small services might actually exhibit 'anti-resilience': the appearance of independence reduces the incentive for each operator to invest in redundancy, because they assume someone else will absorb the failure. This leads to a tragedy of the commons where the entire system becomes fragile. The large service, knowing it cannot externalize the cost, is forced to internalize redundancy.
body.why_keep_this: This inverts the usual assumption that decentralized operators independently provide resilience. It provides a testable economic mechanism rather than a purely technical one.
